diagram_math_checks.result: For simultaneous actions M is an (S,R)-bimodule and N an (R,T)-bimodule. Q=M tensor_R N is initially an abelian-group tensor quotient. Thus s acts on the left of M, t on the right of N, and R is solely the balancing ring. This is the simultaneous handed situation in the Statement and proof 4.1, consistent with def-bimodule.

u_{s,t}:M x N -> M x N sends (m,n) to (sm,nt); tau:M x N -> Q sends (m,n) to m tensor n and is a balanced pairing, not a product-group homomorphism. L_s,R_t:Q -> Q are additive endomorphisms as in steps 1.2 and 2.1, with S relabelled T in the right action. tau after u_{s,t} and (L_s after R_t) after tau both send (m,n) to (sm) tensor (nt).

For r in R, s(mr) tensor (nt) = ((sm)r) tensor (nt) = (sm) tensor r(nt) = (sm) tensor ((rn)t). First and last identities are the respective bimodule commuting laws; middle is the R-balance relation. Additivity in each variable follows from module additivity. By L2/L3 this pairing factors through the tensor quotient Q. The explicit F/H quotient was checked in def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations, via the existing universal-property supplier; no new dependency is introduced.

All four vertices are Q; horizontal maps are R_t and vertical maps L_s, with arrows directed right/down. Both composites send m tensor n to (sm) tensor (nt), exactly proof 4.1. Their additivity and generation by elementary tensors give equality on all Q. This asserts commutation of left S with right T only, and no same-sided scalar commutation or R-linearity.
t=1_T gives the left action, and s=1_S the right action, using unitality. No inverses or commutativity of any ring is assumed.
